name: Lenvatinib
drug_class: Multi-kinase inhibitor (VEGFR1–3, FGFR1–4, PDGFRα, RET, KIT)

discovery.note: A quinoline carboxamide that binds VEGFR2 in a distinct type V mode and also inhibits FGF receptors.

tagline: VEGFR/FGFR inhibitor for thyroid, liver, kidney and endometrial cancer
summary: Lenvatinib is an oral multi-kinase inhibitor of VEGF and FGF receptors, PDGFRα, RET and KIT. It is approved for radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma, and in combination with pembrolizumab for renal cell and endometrial carcinoma.
mechanism: Lenvatinib binds the ATP site and an adjacent region of VEGFR2 (a 'type V' binding mode), giving potent, rapid inhibition of VEGFR1–3 and anti-angiogenic effects.
Inhibition of FGFR1–4 may counter FGF-driven escape from VEGF blockade. Anti-angiogenic remodelling of the tumour microenvironment is thought to enhance responses to PD-1 blockade.
uses: Locally recurrent or metastatic, progressive, radioactive-iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer
Advanced renal cell carcinoma (with pembrolizumab first-line, or with everolimus after anti-angiogenic therapy)
Advanced endometrial carcinoma that is not MSI-high/dMMR (with pembrolizumab)

history.title: Preclinical report
history.detail: Eisai describes E7080 as a VEGFR/FGFR inhibitor.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: SELECT trial leads to approval for radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancer.

history.title: Renal cell carcinoma
history.detail: Approved with everolimus after prior anti-angiogenic therapy.

history.title: Liver cancer and Merck deal
history.detail: REFLECT shows non-inferiority to sorafenib in HCC; Eisai and Merck agree a co-development partnership.

history.title: Endometrial cancer
history.detail: Accelerated approval with pembrolizumab (full approval in 2021 after Study 309/KEYNOTE-775).

history.title: CLEAR
history.detail: FDA approves lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab first-line for advanced renal cell carcinoma.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A and aldehyde oxidase; non-enzymatic

facts: Kisplyx is the EU brand used for the renal cell carcinoma indication.
